Unifolio · Web app · Planning phase

Sign-up, Sign-in and Onboarding Redesign Plan

A screen-by-screen plan for the new login, sign-up and onboarding screens from your two PDFs, up to the point where the user lands on Home. For each screen: how it will look, what changes from today, how we build it, what the backend already supports, and the questions to settle first. This is a UI-only redesign with one approved exception: the onboarding goals need a small backend and database change (Q13), specified in full below.

The short version

The PDFs replace two different looks (a split card for login and sign-up, a small centred card for onboarding) with one continuous split-card flow that runs from sign-in or sign-up through to connecting a first account. Most of what the screens do already exists in code, so the main work is a new presentation layer over the current flows. A few mockup elements depend on behaviour the backend does not have, and the last two screens promise more than the product can deliver today.

9screens drawn in the PDFs (3 login, 6 sign-up)
12groups of screens and states the PDFs do not draw but the flow needs
29 of 29questions answered. All decisions are recorded
1backend change planned, approved: the onboarding goals (Q13). Nothing else (Q9 decided)

What I found, in six points

  1. Two looks today, one in the new design. Today login and sign-up are a split card with an abstract grey illustration and a looping "roadmap" strip, and onboarding is a narrow centred card (screenshots in the Flows section). The PDFs make it one continuous split-card system: a different sketch per screen, a step bar, and green accent words in every headline.
  2. The logic stays, the presentation changes. AuthEntryFlow (647 lines) already holds every sign-up and login API call and branch, and OnboardingFlow holds the onboarding order and resume rules. Both keep their behaviour. The redesign swaps what they render.
  3. Three mockup elements needed a backend we do not have. (a) Email shown as optional: today a phone-first sign-up cannot finish without a verified email. Decided (Q9): the email is compulsory and verified, just as today. (b) Six life goals: the database accepted only four product goals through a CHECK constraint. Decided (Q13): replace the goal enum with the six, with a migration. It has its own section below. (c) "Get code via call": there is no voice delivery and SMS runs in stub mode. Decided (Q4): shown as drawn, with no function for now.
  4. The real flow has more screens than the PDFs. Because email must be verified, a verify-email screen sits between your screens 3 and 4. Screen 5 hosts the whole statement import (choice, CAMS request, waiting, upload, parsing, errors and about a dozen prompts). Error and edge states are not drawn at all. See "Screens without a mockup".
  5. Screens 5 and 6 show things the product cannot do or cannot show truthfully today. Stocks, PMS and Real estate "importing", "MF Central", and "you'll be redirected in a few seconds" while the real import has either already finished or is waiting for an email. Q14 to Q16 are decided. Decided (Q18, Q19): the All set screen shows only real rows, and its button opens Home.
  6. Desktop and mobile share the same two components. Restyling them in place would change the mobile app too. The plan keeps one state machine and gives it two looks (Q20).
Things in the PDFs that looked like mistakes, and how they were settled
  • Step counter. Sign-up screen 1 draws six bar segments but says "Step 1 of 5". Screens 4 and 5 both say "Step 4 of 5". Screen 6 says "Step 5 of 5". Settled (Q7): five steps, All set is the finish.
  • OTP boxes. The sign-up OTP screen draws five boxes while its copy says "6-digit". Login draws six. I build six.
  • Call button on email. "Get code via call" appears on the email verification screen. Settled (Q4): shown as drawn, no function for now.
  • Email masking. The login email screen shows you@e•••••.com. Settled (Q6): the name is partly hidden and the domain shown.
  • Back on the first screen. Settled (Q2): sign-up is the default screen and has no Back. Back on login returns to it.

How this connects to the rest of the app

The auth screens are the front door. Once the user reaches /home, everything is the already-redesigned shell. This section shows where the new screens plug in, and what they hand over.

Decided (Q13): the goal values and labels change in both places, plus the database.
Home and its empty stateThe final destination. Home already has empty-data fixtures.Reached only after an import: onboarding stays mandatory (Q16 decided). The empty state still serves a user who has deleted their data.

Why this matters for the buildThe new screens share three things with the rest of the product: the self household member, the import engine, and the onboarding answers that Profile later displays. Those are the places where a styling-only change can quietly become a behaviour change, so the plan treats them as fixed contracts.

Flows: before and after

How a user moves through sign-in, sign-up and onboarding today, and how they will move after the redesign. The diagrams come from the code, not from the PDFs, so they include steps the PDFs leave out.

Sign-up: before and after

The biggest difference in the flowOrder of name and account. Today the account exists before the name is asked, so the name is saved straight away. In the new order, name and email are asked together on screen 3, before the email is verified and the account created. The name has to be held in the browser until the session exists, then saved. Details in "State, resume and data".

What changes from today

  • Today login is a menu of three buttons. Each opens its own screen, and only then is a field shown. The new screen puts the choice (Email or Mobile number tabs), the field and Get OTP on one screen.
  • The Google button is not in the mockup. Decided (Q1): it is hidden behind one setting and the Google code path stays in the repo.
  • The left panel stops being one shared abstract illustration. This screen and sign-up screen 1 get the laptop sketch with floating asset cards. The code screens get their own sketches.
  • The roadmap strip under the form (the looping line with small icons) goes away on desktop.
  • The logo moves to the top-left of the card and the card gets a Back link in the right panel. Decided (Q2): the app opens on sign-up screen 1, and Back on login returns to it. Sign-up has no Back.

How we build it

Frontend

  • New LoginEntry screen with the tab switch. It calls the existing handleEmailLoginRequest or handlePhoneSubmit directly, so today's separate "email" and "phone" steps are skipped for login. Sign-up already does the same shortcut.
  • New split-card frame (AuthSplitCard) with a left-panel slot and a right-panel slot, reused by every screen in this plan.
  • Existing validators are reused: validateEmail and validateIndianPhone. Existing error mapping stays: "No account found, sign up instead" becomes an inline message with a Sign up link.
  • Left panel content comes from a small config: sketch, headline, paragraph, rows.

Backend

  • Nothing. Email login uses /auth/email-otp/request with flow: login. Mobile login uses /auth/otp/request with flow: login.

Open questions

Q1

What happens to Continue with Google on the login screen?

Answered

Today the login screen offers Google, Email and Phone. The mockup shows only Email and Mobile number. Sign-up already hides Google (the backend path was kept on purpose, "hidden, not removed"). If any real user signed up through Google, they would have no visible way back in once the button is gone.

A. Hide it, keep the codeChosen option

Matches the mockup. A single setting turns the button back on. Safe only if no real user relies on Google.

B. Small "Continue with Google" link under the OR line

Keeps the door open for Google users without crowding the tab design. Not in the PDF.

C. Remove the Google code

Cleaner repo. Hard to undo and breaks the "hidden, not removed" decision.

Recommendation: A. Follow the mockup, keep the component and the backend path behind one flag. Tell me if any real user signed up with Google. If yes, use B.

Q2

Where does Back go on the first login screen?

Answered

The login mockup shows a Back link, the sign-up mockup does not. On desktop the login screen is the first thing a signed-out user sees, so there is no earlier page in the app.

A. Hide it

Nothing sits before it.

B. Link to the marketing site

Back goes to the public Unifolio website. Needs the site address in a setting.

C. Go to sign-up screen 1Chosen option

Behaves like the Sign up link, which makes two links do the same thing.

Recommendation: B if the marketing site has a stable address, otherwise A. I need the address if you choose B.

Q3

Which tab is selected first, and do we remember the last one?

Answered

The mockup opens on Email. Sign-up is phone-first, so most new users think of their number first. A "remember last method" tweak is easy but is not in the PDF.

A. Email first, as drawnChosen option

Follows the PDF.

B. Mobile first

Matches how people sign up.

C. Remember the last used tab

Small browser-storage convenience. Not in the PDF.

Recommendation: A. It is what you drew. C can be added later without redesign.

What changes from today

How we build it

Open questions

Q4

What do we do with "Get code via call"?

Answered

There is no voice-call delivery anywhere in the backend. SMS delivery is also in stub mode today (the code is shown on screen), and email codes go through Amazon SES. The button appears on three screens in the PDFs, including the email one.

A. Leave it out for now

The OR line and grey button are not drawn. The card has a little more space. Add it when voice delivery exists.

B. Draw it disabled with "coming soon"Chosen option

Keeps the design. A disabled button on a security screen invites support questions.

C. Build voice OTP

A provider, backend route, cost and abuse limits. A separate project.

Recommendation: A, on all three screens. A control that does nothing on a login screen costs more trust than the empty space. The layout works without it. The email screen should never have it.

Q5

How does the resend countdown behave?

Answered

The mockup shows "Resend code in 00:28". The backend allows one new code per 60 seconds per number and answers 429 "Please wait Ns" otherwise. Today there is a plain "Resend code" link with no timer.

A. Start at 01:00, link becomes active at zeroChosen option

Matches the backend rule. A 429 still shows the server's own message.

B. Start at 00:30

Shorter wait than the backend allows, so a tap would often fail.

C. No timer

Keep today's plain link.

Recommendation: A. The 28 seconds in the PDF is just a sample value.

Q6

How are the phone number and email masked?

Answered

The PDF masks the phone as +91 ••••• 43210 (last 5 digits shown) and the email as you@e•••••.com, which hides the domain and shows the name. For the user to recognise which address received the code, the common pattern is to hide part of the name and show the full domain.

A. Phone: keep last 5. Email: keep first 2 letters of the name and the full domain (si••••••@gmail.com)Chosen option

Recognisable and private.

B. Exactly as drawn

Email pattern is unusual and the domain is the most useful clue.

C. Show in full

Simplest. Shows personal data on a screen that may be shared in a screenshot.

Recommendation: A. Phone follows the PDF. Only the email rule changes.

Q7

How do the six screens map to "Step N of 5"?

Answered

Sign-up draws six screens: mobile, code, account, profile, connect, all set. The labels say Step 1 of 5, 2 of 5, 3 of 5, then "4 of 5" on both profile and connect, then "5 of 5" on all set. Screen 1 draws six bar segments, the others five. The real flow also has a verify-email screen after screen 3.

A. Five steps, all set is the finishChosen option

1 Mobile, 2 Code, 3 Account (the email check is a sub-step of it, same number), 4 Profile, 5 Connect. All set shows all five bars full and the label "Done" instead of a step number.

B. Six steps

Every drawn screen counts: "Step 1 of 6" to "Step 6 of 6". Honest to the screens, different from the PDF text.

C. Copy the PDF labels exactly

Repeats the 4-of-5 twice and the six-segment bar on screen 1. Looks like a bug.

Recommendation: A. It keeps the "5" you drew, fixes the doubled 4, and treats finishing as the end of the bar rather than a sixth step. I need your confirmation because it changes the labels on two screens.

Amended 2 Nov (Round 3): Q7 is unchanged. The path from Connect accounts to All set is now drawn and specified as one flow: Round 3, B (Q63, Q64).

Does the mobile field need a country drop-down?

Answered

What changes from today

  • Name and email now share one screen. Today the name is asked after the account exists (the "What should we call you?" screen), and the email is asked on its own "One more step" screen before that.
  • The order of account creation shifts. The name is typed before the account exists, so it is held in the browser until the session is created, then saved as the self member. If the browser is refreshed in between, the name is asked again (see "State, resume and data").
  • The name rules stay: validatePersonName and the PAN wording. The placeholder "Siddharth Surve" reads like a real person, so please confirm you are happy to use it publicly.
  • The PDF draws the email field as optional. Decided (Q9): it is compulsory and verified, just as today.
  • Decided (Q10): Back from screen 4 shows this screen with the name and the email both read-only, and Continue simply moves on.
  • Decided (Q11): the Terms and Privacy line is not repeated here. It lives on screen 1, where the agreement is recorded.

How we build it

Frontend

  • New AccountDetails screen replacing the "One more step" email screen and the name screen (Q1Name). It is shown inside AuthEntryFlow when verifyOtp returns email_required.
  • On Continue it calls the existing handleEmailGateSubmit(email) and keeps the typed name in a small session-scoped store (pendingSignup).
  • When the session appears, OnboardingFlow finds the stored name, calls createHouseholdMember(name, "self") once, clears the store and goes straight to screen 4.
  • If there is no stored name (the user refreshed), resumeStep already returns the name step because self_name is empty. The screen then shows only the name field with the verified email read-only.

Backend

  • Nothing. Same /auth/email-otp/request, /auth/email-otp/verify and /household-members calls. The order the frontend makes them in does not matter to the backend.

Holding the name until the session existsNewFrontend session storage.
"Encrypted and protected" statementKept as drawnDecided 2 Nov (Q11). Only the PAN and the stored statement are confirmed encrypted, so keep the wording accurate before release.

Open questions

Q9

Is the email optional, as drawn?

Answered

The PDF labels the email "(optional)" and has no email check. The backend does not work that way. A phone-first sign-up returns email_required after the phone code, and the account is created only when the email code is verified (complete_gated_signup). So with the backend as it is, an empty email cannot create an account.

A. Email required and verified. UI onlyChosen option

Drop "(optional)" from the label, add the verify-email screen 3b. No backend change. Differs from the PDF.

B. Email optional, no verification

Matches the PDF. Needs a backend change: a way to finish phone-first sign-up without an email, plus a later way to add one. This breaks the "UI only" rule.

C. Email optional but verified if given

Same backend change as B, plus the check.

Recommendation: A. It is the only option that keeps the promise of no backend change. B can be a separate, small backend task later. If you want B, tell me and I will scope the backend part separately.

Q10

What happens to the name when the user presses Back from screen 4?

Answered

The self member is saved when the session is created. Going Back to screen 3 then shows a name that already exists as a household member. Editing it means updating that member, and an email that has just been verified should not be editable.

A. Show name editable, email read-only

On Continue, update the existing self member (an update call already exists) instead of creating another.

B. Show both read-onlyChosen option

Simplest, but a typo in the PAN name is then fixable only from Profile.

C. Skip screen 3 on Back and go to screen 1

Confusing: the account already exists.

Recommendation: A. The update call exists (updateMemberProfile). The PAN name matters for matching, so a typo should be fixable right here.

Amended 2 Nov (Round 3): Both fields are now editable on Back, and a changed email gets a new code and replaces the old one: Round 3, C (Q65, Q66). The chosen option above is replaced.

Q11

The new lines under Continue: second consent line and the "encrypted" claim

Answered

Consent is recorded at the Get OTP click on screen 1. Screen 3 repeats "By continuing, you agree to our Terms and Privacy Policy" under Continue, which can read as if consent is given here. The same block says "Your data is encrypted and protected".

A. Keep both lines as drawn

Follows the PDF. The second consent line is informational only.

B. Keep the encryption line, drop the repeat consent lineChosen option

Avoids two moments that look like consent.

C. Reword the consent line to "You agreed to our Terms and Privacy Policy"

Accurate to what happened. Not in the PDF.

Recommendation: C, with the encryption wording checked first. Please confirm what is encrypted (PAN is, per ADR-004) before a blanket claim goes on screen. This is a legal and security wording call that only you can sign off.

What changes from today

  • Two screens become one. Today the investing screen (how you invest) and the purpose screen (what brings you) are separate screens with a Skip each. The PDF puts both on one screen with a single Continue and no Skip.
  • The goals change meaning. Today's four options are about what the user wants from Unifolio. The PDF's six are life goals. Decided (Q13): the stored goal values are replaced by the six. The full backend and database change is in "New goals: backend and database".

How we build it

Frontend

  • New InvestorProfile replacing Q2Investing and Q3Purpose. One updateMe({investor_type, primary_goals}) call on Continue.
  • Wording lives in profile-v2/lib/onboardingOptions.ts, which Profile already uses. Changing it there keeps Profile and sign-up in step.
  • Step names in onboardingSteps.ts stay as they are. The merged screen writes q2_investing and reads either old value on resume, so people already mid-onboarding are not stranded (see "State, resume and data").

Backend

  • Nothing for the investor type. The six life goals need an enum, schema and migration change (Q13), described in full in "New goals: backend and database".

Answered

The PDF shows "Just getting started" and "Wealth creation" already selected, and has no Skip. PRD-02 FR-7 says every onboarding question must be skippable or deferrable, and FR-7a says a skipped question must be revisitable. A pre-selected answer saves data the user never chose.

The data path, before and after

Database change in detail

One Alembic migration does three things in this order: clear any saved goals, swap the Postgres CHECK, then drop the deprecated primary_goal column and its enum type. The code below is the shape, not final code.

revision = "<next free number>"      # 0053 today (see the numbering note below)
down_revision = "<head at build time>"

_NEW = '["wealth_creation","retirement","childrens_education","buy_home","financial_freedom","tax_planning"]'
_OLD = '["consolidated_view","understand_holdings","family_management","performance_comparison"]'


def upgrade() -> None:
    is_pg = op.get_bind().dialect.name == "postgresql"

    # 1. No old value maps onto a new goal, so any saved answer is cleared.
    #    On the cleared staging database this changes zero rows.
    op.execute("UPDATE users SET primary_goals = NULL")

    # 2. Postgres only: swap the CHECK for the six new codes, 1 to 6 items.
    if is_pg:
        op.drop_constraint("ck_users_primary_goals_allowed", "users", type_="check")
        op.create_check_constraint(
            "ck_users_primary_goals_allowed", "users",
            "primary_goals IS NULL OR CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(primary_goals) = 'array'"
            f" THEN jsonb_array_length(primary_goals) BETWEEN 1 AND 6 AND primary_goals <@ '{_NEW}'::jsonb"
            " ELSE false END",
        )

    # 3. Finish the contract step 0019 promised: drop the single-goal column,
    #    then (Postgres) its native enum type. The type cannot be dropped first.
    with op.batch_alter_table("users") as batch:
        batch.drop_column("primary_goal")
    if is_pg:
        op.execute("DROP TYPE IF EXISTS primarygoal")


def downgrade() -> None:
    # Recreate the type, the column and the old CHECK. New values cannot be
    # represented in the old shape, so saved goals are cleared first.
    ...
Why the old column is dropped instead of changedusers.primary_goal is a native Postgres enum, and Postgres cannot remove values from an enum. Changing it means recreating the type and rewriting the column. The column has been deprecated since 30 Sep, and nothing reads it. Only the dual write in update_me touches it. So the cleanest fix is the drop the 0019 note already promised. Tell me if you would rather keep the column.
Migration numberingThe change-requests runs on the same branch have claimed 0047 to 0052 (Head of Family is 0050 to 0052). This migration takes the next free number, 0053 at the time of writing. Check alembic heads before creating it.

Open question

Q13b

How many goals can be picked, and does "All of it" stay?

Answered

The PDF's goals question said "(Select up to 3)", but your copy slide replaced that heading and did not restate the limit. Today the database allows up to four goals and the onboarding and Profile screens have an "All of it" shortcut that selects everything. With six goals, that shortcut and a limit of 3 cannot coexist. The migration, the schema bound and the dialogs above are written for up to 3.

A. Up to 3, no "All of it"

Matches the PDF. CHECK allows 1 to 3 items. The shortcut and the "All of it" chip are removed.

B. Up to 6, keep "All of it"Chosen option

Any combination. CHECK allows 1 to 6. The shortcut selects all six and Profile can still show "All of it".

C. Up to 3 on sign-up, any number in Profile

Different rules in two places. More code, more confusion.

Recommendation: A. It is what the PDF drew, and a short list of goals is more useful for personalisation than all six. Only the bound in the CHECK, the schema constant and the dialogs change if you choose B.

1 · Greeting follows the selected member

Home

A small server fix. The greeting should name the person whose numbers are on screen.

What you asked for

On Home, in the family view the greeting shows the head of the family's name. When you switch to one member, the name does not change. It should show that member's first name.

What the code does today

Read from the leapswitch-redesign branch at bd8cd19, on 2 Nov 2026.

  • The greeting text comes from greetingLine(summary.greeting, summary.display_name) in features/home/homeFormat.ts, drawn by features/home/sections/Greeting.tsx.
  • display_name is built by _display_name(db, user.id) in backend/app/api/home.py. That function takes only the user. It picks the member whose relationship is self, or the first member if none is self, and returns the first word of the name in title case.
  • The endpoint already resolves the scope (a member id, or all) with resolve_scope and passes ctx.member_name into the summary. So the selected member is known on the server. _display_name just ignores it.
Cause, in one line

The backend function that builds the name never looks at which member is selected. It always returns the head of the family. This is a backend bug, not a frontend one.

Your family's portfolio is up ₹5,548 today.

Aditi's portfolio is up ₹1,210 today.

  • Check that switching the view refetches the summary. The home page already keys its requests on the member id, so the new name arrives with the new data. A test confirms it.

Backend

  • api/home.py: _display_name gets the resolved scope. In the family view it keeps today's rule (self, else first member). With one member selected it uses that member.
  • The call in _summary changes from _display_name(db, user.id) to pass ctx. ctx.member_name is already loaded, so no extra query is needed for the member case.
  • Keep the same cleaning: first word of the name, title case. A member whose name is empty falls back to the head of the family.

None.

  • Frontend: Greeting.test.tsx and HomePage.test.tsx render both views and check the heading text changes when the scope changes.

Edge cases

  • A member with a long or hyphenated first word (for example Mary-Anne) is shown as the first word only, as today.
  • A member with no data still gets their name. The greeting does not depend on holdings.
  • After change 5 the head of the family can have no data. In the family view the greeting still shows the head's name (Q29).

3c · The benchmark named in the Inception table

The pills are drawn for every source in 3 · UI and every state.

  • The system already exists for the graph and the block under the table. It chooses the factsheet's benchmark when it can be built, then the closest index we hold, then the category's index, and says which. This part reuses it. It adds nothing to how the benchmark is chosen. Change-requests Run 3 is executed first and its final rules apply.
  • Frontend: under the row label Benchmark two small pills: the index name (benchmarkDisplayName turns TRI into Total Return) in a neutral pill, and the source in a pill coloured by kind: From the factsheet (green), Closest index we hold (blue), Chosen by category (amber), As printed in the factsheet (dashed, for the printed-returns case with BENCHMARK_PRINTED_LABEL). The words come from lib/benchmarkDisplay.ts, so the pills, the block under the table and the graph legend cannot say different things. One small BenchmarkPills component is used by the Inception row and the Current row.
  • Backend: add benchmark_label (the index's display name) to ReturnsResponse for both modes, from the same BENCHMARK_LABELS lookup the performance response uses. The frontend already reads this field.
  • The block under the table stays as it is. It carries the note text from the backend (for example when the benchmark's history starts late). The row bracket is a short form of it.
  • If the benchmark cannot be named, the pills are left out and the row reads Benchmark as today.

Tests

  • Backend: ReturnsResponse.benchmark_label is present for both modes. A test for each source value: factsheet, closest, category, none.
  • Backend: the /performance and /returns responses keep every existing field exactly as today, so nothing else moves.
  • Frontend: every bar equals its table cell, for a sample response and a synthetic one. A period with no figure draws no bars and shows a dash. A negative XIRR draws a bar below the baseline. A missing benchmark row gives one series. Changing the scope refetches once and updates the graph and the table together.
  • Frontend: the existing PerformanceChart tests pass unedited. The Inception view renders the same markup as before, apart from the slot with the toggle. The benchmark row shows the right pills for each source value.
  • A before and after screenshot of the Inception view at 1440 and 1024: identical except the toggle row in the performance card. Screenshots of every state drawn in the UI section.
  • Real-statement check: the bars against the Current table for a real fund, including a statement with an opening balance (the table's own maths already handles it).

Edge cases

  • The user holds the fund in some members but not the selected one. The table says not held. The graph card shows its own not-held state (Q56).
  • The holding is shorter than a period. The table dashes that cell. The graph shows no bars for it and a dash.
  • A negative XIRR draws a bar below the baseline, and the axis includes the negative range.
  • Very different sizes, for example 120% against 5%. The axis scales to the larger one and the small bar is short but still labelled. The implementation plan checks how the chart crowds its labels.
  • No benchmark data: one series, a short notice, and the table hides its benchmark row.
  • The user sold everything. The table's rule applies, and the bars show whatever the table shows.
  • Switching the toggle fast: the pending Current request is cancelled, as the other sections do with their abort signal.

3 · UI and every state

Individual fund · Overview

The refined design for the toggle, the Current graph, the benchmark pills and the states around them, in the app's own look.

What this section is

A cleaner, more polished design for the new parts of change 3, with the Current view drawn as grouped bars (Q59), in the app's own dark look (taken from your Returns screenshots) with its real tokens, and one mockup for every state. It replaces the first, plainer drawings and the bracket wording. All figures are samples.

Rules this design keeps

  • The existing graph is not changed. The Inception view's chart, legend, colours, notes and period buttons are drawn exactly as they are today.
  • The new Current graph is a grouped bar chart from the app's existing chart set, in the same card, colours and legend format as that graph, so switching the toggle does not change the style of the page. It has no period buttons, because every period is on the chart.
  • The polish goes into what is new: the toggle row and its spacing, the benchmark pills, and the empty, loading and error states.
  • The Returns table keeps today's density and columns. Only the benchmark label cell gains pills.
  • Everything uses the app's tokens (--ui-elevated, --ui-divider, --ui-text, --ui-text-muted, --ui-hover, --pos-text, --neg-text, --c2, --c3), so light mode follows without a second design.

Read from the leapswitch-redesign branch at bd8cd19, on 2 Nov 2026.

  • The table is features/mutual-funds/overlap/TopPairs.tsx: columns #, Fund 1, Fund 2, Overlap (bar and percent), Shared Stocks, Combined Weight. It is shown by OverlapTab.tsx through local state (compareWith), so it has no URL of its own today.
  • Routes today: /portfolio/mutual-funds/funds/:schemeId/overlap (individual) and /portfolio/mutual-funds/overlap (portfolio). No compare route exists.

What happens to the combined weight calculation

  • The table stops using it. TopPairs.tsx no longer calls combinedWeight and no longer shows the value.

A search of the frontend finds it used in overlapLogic.ts (lines 166 to 167) inside the logic that builds the Key insights sentences (together they account for 20% of your portfolio). Removing it would break that text. The implementation plan re-confirms this by reading those lines before anything is deleted.
  • Nothing on the server does this calculation. It is computed in the browser from each pair's values and total_portfolio_value, which other cards also use. So there is no backend work to stop.

5 · Name mismatch: add as a family member

First upload · onboarding

The biggest change in round 2. The account holder is never renamed. The uploaded people become family members.

What you asked for

When the first statement is in a different name from the name typed at sign-up, the pop-up should not rename the account holder. It should say whose account it is, whose file was uploaded, and offer Add [name] as a family member or Upload a different file. The account holder stays the head of the family (self) with no data yet. The people in the file are added as family members, and the normal flow continues. If the account holder is in the file, they stay the head and get those funds.

What the code does today

Read from the leapswitch-redesign branch at bd8cd19, on 2 Nov 2026.

  • Backend, services/import_/service.py (around line 593): on a first upload, _self_match compares the typed name with every person in the file (resolve_self in people_resolution.py: by PAN once the PAN is permanent, else by exact or variant name). No match returns the prompt self_name_mismatch with entered_name and statement_name. Several matches return which_is_self.
  • The answer to that prompt, resolve_name (line 869), renames the self member to the statement's name, records a HouseholdMemberNameChange (reason USER_CORRECTED_TO_CAS), sets the name source to CAS and continues. This is the behaviour you want to stop.
  • Frontend: features/import/prompts/NameMismatchDialog.tsx shows This statement is in X's name. You entered Y. Is that you? with Yes, that's me and Upload a different file. PromptHost.tsx sends {kind: "name"} to resolve.
  • The engine already supports a file that has no one matching the account holder. A code comment says an Add-data upload of a relative's statement has no Me (F11). And plan_people already plans every other person in a file as new, and confirm_people.py (line 586) creates new members with relationship=None. That fits your plan: relation is filled in later.
  • Profile completion: members carry profile_completion and features/dashboard/members/CompleteProfileDialog is the existing pop-up where relation and other details are filled. Home already labels a member No data yet (Greeting.tsx, has_data).
  • Onboarding uploads through SoloCasUpload.tsx, which passes the self member as the upload target.

Backend

  • service.py: the self_name_mismatch prompt details stay as they are (entered_name, statement_name). A new resolver, resolve_add_as_family, next to resolve_name: it sets a session flag (for example session['add_as_family']) and continues. It does not touch the self member's name, name source or PAN, and writes no HouseholdMemberNameChange.
  • With the flag set, _self_match is skipped for the rest of the session, so no me_key is chosen. plan_people then marks everyone as new (or existing_member/other_account by PAN, as today).
  • Check every later step for an assumption that the first upload contains Me: the self claim in _advance, the PAN claims, member_not_in_file for the self target, the cross_account_pan_blocked shortcut (F30, which today exempts the case where Me is one of the people), the onboarding onboarding_completed write, and the coverage and opening-balance checks. The F11 comment suggests this path exists for Add-data uploads. It must be proved for a first upload with the self member as target.
  • The import is saved against the upload target. The funds must be attached to the new members, not to the self member the upload was started for. confirm_people.py already attaches each person's funds to that person's member. This must be confirmed in the implementation plan with a test.
  • The API route for the answer (resolve) gets the new kind. Old clients that still send name get the old behaviour until the frontend ships, then the old path is removed (Q39).
  • Head of Family. The whole change-requests plan, Runs 5 and 6 included, is executed before this starts (Q40, Q51). This page says self member for the account holder. If Head of Family changed how that member is stored or found, the new resolver follows the new rule. Step 0 re-reads those files, and the tests in this section are written against them.

A file with several people

  • Same pop-up and same flow as today. The pop-up names the person the statement is in (the name it uses today). It does not list everyone and has no extra buttons.
  • After Add {name} as a family member, the normal steps continue unchanged: the existing people-found step offers the other people in the file, then the scheme match and confirm steps. Nothing new is built for several people.
  • If the account holder is one of the people in the file, there is no mismatch and no pop-up. They stay the head of the family and get their funds, as today.

Database

  • No schema change is expected. New members already use the existing household_members columns, with relationship empty. PAN storage (encrypted, per member, with a lookup hash) already exists.
  • The self member keeps pan_lookup_hash empty and name_source = USER_ENTERED. When Prateek later uploads his own file, resolve_self falls back to name matching because his PAN is not yet permanent, and classify_detected_pan must not say his PAN belongs to another member. This is the Q38 case and needs its own test.
  • One thing to confirm: the PAN-claim record (pending_claims) for the first upload. If a claim is created for the self member by mistake, Prateek's PAN would later look taken. The new path must create claims only for the new members.
  • If the import record needs to remember that no one in it was the account holder, that is a flag on the session, not a column.

Tests

  • Backend: first upload, one different person: prompt shows people, add_as_family creates one member, self name unchanged, no name-change row, funds on the new member. Several people: all become members. Account holder in the file: unchanged behaviour (matched, no prompt). Upload a different file: nothing saved. Later upload of the account holder's own file: matched by name, then PAN stored on Prateek, not on Lalchand.
  • Backend: a regression run of the existing synthetic CAS set (Docs/CAS Files/synthetic) in normal and mfapi-blocked modes, as the repo's gate does, since this touches the import service.
  • Frontend: dialog copy and buttons, one and several people, the new resolve kind in PromptHost, Complete profile pop-up after confirm, Home with a no-data head of family.
  • Real-file check: one real statement uploaded under a different typed name, as the repo does for import changes.

Edge cases

  • A typo in the typed name (Pratek). The old flow fixed it with Yes, that's me. The new flow offers to add the account holder as a new family member instead. This is why Q39 asks for a third option.
  • The file's person already exists as a family member by exact name. find_member_by_exact_name attaches to that member, as today.
  • The file's PAN already belongs to another Unifolio account. The existing cross-account block applies.
  • Everyone in the file is a minor or has no PAN. The existing needs name handling applies.
  • The user adds Lalchand, then also uploads Prateek's file in the same onboarding. Onboarding completes after the first import, so the second upload is done later from Add data, for the head of the family.

8 · New funds and their transactions after an upload

Import result · notice · history

Show which funds are new, with their invested amount, latest date and transactions, next to the existing counts.

What you asked for

After an upload for a later month, the app says N funds detected, X skipped, Y added. Wherever that is shown, also show a table for the new funds: fund name, amount and date. Your later answers: amount is the invested amount and the date is the latest transaction (Q47); and on 2 Nov you asked for a cleaner design that also shows the new funds and the new transactions of those funds.

What the code does today

Read from the leapswitch-redesign branch at bd8cd19, on 2 Nov 2026.

  • features/import/useImportOrchestration.tsx builds the notice from ImportConfirmResponse: per person X added, Y already saved and a total N transactions added · M already saved.

  • The same wording appears in ImportHistoryList.tsx (duplicate_transactions_count), and the import preview lists schemes (SchemeMatchPreview) before confirm.
  • A new fund is a scheme the member held no units of before this upload (Q46). That is worked out on the server from existing data.
About your question, is that what we count now?

No. Today's numbers count transactions (rows in the statement), not funds. A repeat of an October upload shows the same transactions as already saved. A fund bought for the first time in December shows only as more transactions added. Nothing tells the user which funds are new. That is the gap this change fills.

When it shows, and for whom

  • Money is shown with the app's existing rupee formatter. Dates use the existing date formatter.

Backend

  • confirm_people.py and the confirm response in schemas.py: add new_funds per person, each with its transactions (capped at 20, with the full count in transaction_count).
  • How to find new funds without storing anything new: for each scheme in this import, it is new if the member's folios held no units of it before this import's first transaction for that scheme. This is a read on transactions grouped by scheme, filtered by import_id (Q46).
  • Invested amount and latest date (Q47): the invested amount is the total of the purchase-type transactions of that scheme in this import. Whether redemptions in the same statement are netted off is confirmed when the transaction types are read. The date is the latest transaction date of that scheme in this import.
  • Import History reads the same data later through a read-only endpoint for one import (working name GET /imports/{import_id}/new-funds), derived the same way. No new table or column.
  • Existing users only (Q70). For the sign-up upload the confirm skips the new-funds work and returns an empty list, so the response stays small and no query runs. The in-app imports return the list.
  • All money maths uses Decimal.

Database

No migration. The new funds and their transactions are derived when they are read, from transactions and imports (Q46). On Postgres the transactions table is partitioned by year, so the query filters by the import's date range.

Tests

  • Backend: first upload (all funds new, with their transactions), a later upload with one new fund and many repeats (only that fund listed, only its transactions), a repeat of the same file (empty list, already_imported unchanged), two members in one file (separate lists), a fund sold fully before and bought again (not new), and a fund with more than 20 transactions (capped, count correct).
  • Backend: the History endpoint returns the same funds as the confirm response did, for the same import.
  • Frontend: the tiles, the collapsed rows, an opened row, the collapsible section header, the empty state, and the notice with its link. The three places render the same component.
  • Backend and frontend: the sign-up upload returns no list and renders no section. Add data and Add Investment return and render it. The section collapses and expands from the keyboard. A statement with 40 new funds lists all 40.
  • Synthetic CAS gate re-run, since confirm is shared with the import checks.

Edge cases

  • Several purchases of the same new fund in one statement: one row per fund, the invested amount is their total, the date is the latest.
  • A fund that is new but only has a redemption or zero units in the statement (an old closed fund): probably not listed as new.
  • The same fund held by two family members: new for one, not for the other. The list is per person.
  • A fund whose name is long: the row truncates it and the full name is in its tooltip.
  • Hide-values mode, if it applies on this page, hides the rupee amounts.
  • An existing user adds the first statement for a family member who has no data: every fund is new, so the list is long. It stays one collapsible section.
  • A user who finishes sign-up and then uses Add data the same day is an existing user from then on and sees the list for that second upload.

C · Name and email editable on Back, with a new code for a new email (Q10 amended, Q65, Q66)

What you asked for

When the user goes Back from the investor profile to screen 3, both the name and the email are editable. If they change the email on coming back, a new code is generated and the email is sent to the new address. That email is then used and stored for the user.

What the code does today

Read from the leapswitch-redesign branch at bd8cd19, on 2 Nov 2026.

  • backend/app/api/auth.py already has POST /auth/contact-change/request and POST /auth/contact-change/verify for a signed-in user. Request checks the new address is available (_assert_contact_available), then sends a code to that new address through the same email provider as the sign-up code, with the same 60-second throttle.
  • Verify checks the code, then replaces the user's email identity with the new address (the identity's subject is changed, or the old identity is deleted if the new one already exists), sets users.email, marks it verified, and returns the user. So the new email is used for sign-in and stored for the user, and the old one stops working.
  • Screen 3 has already created the account (the email code was verified before screen 4). The user is signed in on Back, so these endpoints apply.
  • The household member's name is changed with the existing member update (updateMemberProfile), as planned in Q10 option A.

Execution strategy

All round 2 changes and the auth redesign

The cleanest way to build everything with the Claude-Codex method this repo already uses, in an order that avoids collisions and keeps every stage reviewable and undoable.

The short answer

Build in eight stages with the same loop used for Sub-projects 1 and 2 and the analytics fixes, now with two workers: Claude orchestrates, writes one handoff per task, verifies and commits; Codex implements and self-checks all backend tasks; Antigravity implements and self-checks all frontend tasks; every stage ends with a mandatory adversarial review. Each stage is one run, with its own start commit, its own Codex clone, its own gate and its own tag. Order the stages by the files they share and by risk. Only tasks that share no files run side by side. This costs more tokens than one big pass. It is the cleanest, because a problem is found in the stage that caused it and any stage can be undone on its own.

Team and where the branch stands (3 Nov 2026)

There is no manager in the loop: the owner and Claude run every stage. Codex = backend, Antigravity = frontend, Claude = orchestrator. Each task in the implementation plan carries a tag [Codex], [Antigravity] or [Claude]. A stage with both lanes runs them at the same time: the backend handoff gives the exact response shape, and the frontend builds against it. Each worker has one rules file (ui-common-rules-codex.md, ui-common-rules-antigravity.md) and neither runs a git command that changes anything. The owner pastes each prompt and each report between Claude and the worker. Claude’s session cannot push (its git proxy refuses this repo), so Claude commits locally and the owner pushes.

The branch is at 6d7c84f: Runs 1 to 6 of the change-requests plan are done, the Alembic head is 0052, and Run 7 (frontend) is still open and goes first. S0 starts after Run 7 is tagged.

Why not one big pass

  • The repo records that skipping the whole-release review of the Individual Fund release was a named risk (CLAUDE.md, owner decisions OD1 to OD4). One review over nine changes plus the auth redesign would repeat that.
  • Several changes edit the same files (see the table below). Side by side they collide. In the right order they do not.
  • The Head of Family work (Runs 5 and 6 of the change-requests plan) changes who the account holder is and adds a migration. The whole change-requests plan is executed first (Q40, Q51), so every stage is written against that final code, and Step 0 re-reads it.

The method, step by step

Taken from the "Method: the Claude-Codex loop" section of Docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-change-requests-implementation-plan.md and the model-orchestration skill. A stage here is what a run is there.

Part of the loopWhat happens in this plan
RolesClaude (orchestrator): interface design, the backend contract, migrations, handoff documents, verification, commits, merges, reviews, the docs update. Codex through codex:codex-rescue: all backend tasks, one handoff at a time, self-checks. Antigravity (Gemini 4 “Argon”, then Gemini 3.8 high): all frontend tasks, one handoff at a time, checks through the WSL check script. A Claude subagent only under the three conditions in references/delegation-rules.md. The model is never switched without your say.
Before any dispatchRecord the start commit on leapswitch-redesign. Clone it at that commit into a fresh directory on the native filesystem (~/ui-s1 and so on) with a throwaway branch codex/ui-s1. Run the cheap probe first (write a one-line file, git add, git commit). If Git writes fail there, Codex implements and self-checks and the orchestrator does every staging, commit and merge. Provision backend/.venv and frontend/node_modules in the clone only after the probe.
Handoff documentsOne per task, or per group of tasks that share files, at Docs/orchestration/ui-s1-<slug>-handoff.md, in the repo's handoff template. Status OPEN, IN REVIEW, DONE. The handoff points at the section of this plan and does not restate it. One line per decision goes in Docs/orchestration/delegation-log.md.
Implementation plansAfter you say go, each stage gets a written plan in Docs/superpowers/plans/ in the same format as the change-requests plan (tasks, failing tests, signatures, verify commands).
Per task: the standard cycle1 failing tests, named, with assertions. 2 run them and confirm they fail for the stated reason. 3 implement the stated signatures. 4 run the task's test files. 5 the orchestrator reads git diff --stat and the changed files, re-runs the touched tests and commits with the prefix ui-s<N>:.
Parallel dispatchOnly for tasks that share no files, stated per stage. Otherwise one after another.
Review gate before DONE/codex:adversarial-review over <start commit>..HEAD, through codex:codex-rescue with run_in_background: true, never in a worktree. The wrapper only forwards, so the owner types /codex:status <id> and /codex:result <id> and relays the output. I will say so each time a review is sent. Findings are never applied automatically. A verdict that contradicts a direct read of the cited lines is sent again. Small fixes may be made by the orchestrator under the skill's review-loop rules, followed by a scoped re-review. Stop when what is left is lower severity, safe and would need a bigger build: record it as a known limit.
Verification tieringIntermediate rounds re-run only the touched tests. The round expected to finish a stage, and any round that touches shared code, runs the full backend and frontend suites.
Deeper checkMoney and data-safety stages (S3 and S5) get a second, scoped review round after fixes and a hand check of every figure. Opus is considered only if one of the three named triggers fires, and only if you approve.
Stage gate, in orderTouched tests; full suites; npm run build and npm run lint; old-payload tests; then the stage checks below. Then tag ui-s<N>-done, add the delegation-log line and update session.md.

Undoing a stage

  • Each stage is a run of commits with the prefix ui-s<N>: and one tag. Reverting that range removes the stage and leaves the others alone.
  • The auth redesign has its own switch: the variant prop in App.tsx (plan section 8).
  • The goals migration has a tested downgrade. Staging data is cleared before it ships, so there is nothing to convert.

Where tokens are saved, and where they are not

Saved, with no loss of qualitySpent on purpose, for cleanliness
  • The handoff points at this page's section and does not restate it.
  • git diff --stat before reading any diff.
  • Intermediate rounds re-run only the touched tests. The full suite runs at the gate.
  • Tasks run side by side only on files that do not overlap, so there is no merge repair.
  • One fresh clone per stage, not per task.
  • One independent review per stage, not one for everything.
  • Failing tests first, always.
  • Real-file and real-data checks and a second review round on S3 and S5, and a real-statement check on S4.
  • Screenshots against the plan mockups on every screen change.
  • A scoped re-review after every fix.

Before anything starts (S0)

  • Everything is answered, and the goal codes are approved. Nothing is open.
  • Tell me when the change-requests plan is fully executed, and give me the start commit.
  • Nothing is built until you say go.

Resume: old step values to new screens

The onboarding_step column is a free text field, so no migration is needed. The new flow reads the four old values and writes only values that already exist.

Saved onboarding_stepToday lands onNew flow lands onNote
(none) or sign-up not finishedNameScreen 3 (name only, email read-only), or screen 1 if signed outResume rule: past the name step with no saved name goes back to name.
q1_nameNameScreen 3Written when screen 3's account exists but no name is saved yet.
q2_investingHow are you investingScreen 4 with answers filledWritten when screen 4 is shown.
q3_purposeWhat brings youScreen 4 with answers filledSame screen as q2 now. Old value still read.

trust_primer (old, removed 1 Oct)First unanswered questionSame rule, ending on screen 4 or 5Existing special case stays.

Edge cases to cover in tests

  • Refresh between the email code being accepted and the name being saved: the session exists, no name is stored, resumeStep returns the name step, screen 3 shows the name field with the email read-only.
  • A second person signs in on the same tab while a pending name is stored: the stored phone does not match, so the name is ignored and cleared.
  • Self member created twice (React strict mode, double click): the list-then-create guard in SoloCasUpload and the new save point both check for an existing self member first.
  • A user mid-onboarding when this ships (saved step q3_purpose) sees screen 4 with their earlier answers filled.
  • Skip for now on screen 4 (Q12): both fields stay empty, Profile shows empty rows, and Profile can set them later.

Open questions

Q26

How are people already mid-onboarding handled when this ships?

Answered

Staging is in multi-user testing, and testers may be partway through today's flow. The saved step values are free text, so nothing breaks, but a tester on q3_purpose lands on the new combined screen.

A. Map old values to the new screens, as in the tableChosen option

No data loss. Answers appear filled in.

B. Restart onboarding for everyone

Simpler, loses answers.

C. Keep both flows until staging is wiped

More code for a short-lived case.

Recommendation: A. It is three lines in resumeStep and the staging database is wiped regularly anyway.

Open questions

Q27

How is it built and rolled out?

Answered

Desktop and mobile share two big components, and the redesign should not break either while staging testers are using the app.

A. New components beside the old ones, switched by a variant propChosen option

Old look stays for mobile. Desktop switches in one place. Easy to compare and to roll back.

B. Rewrite in place

No duplicate code, but mobile changes at the same time as desktop.

C. A feature flag that shows the new look to chosen testers first

Safest. Needs a flag mechanism the repo does not have.

Recommendation: A. Add C later only if you want testers split. A small variant flip in App.tsx is also the rollback.

Round 2 phases

The build order for round 2 and the auth redesign is now one plan, in Execution strategy. It replaces the three phases that were listed here.

Q28

What order do we build in?

Answered

The login screens are the smallest and reuse the code screens that sign-up also needs. Sign-up has the most open questions.

A. Foundations, login, sign-up front, sign-up backChosen option

Lowest risk first. A usable login early.

B. Sign-up first

New users matter most, but it needs the most decisions answered.

C. A clickable skeleton of all nine screens first

Lets you click through everything early with fake data, then fill in.

Recommendation: A, with C's idea inside Phase 1. Phase 1 ends with every screen reachable from a dev-only index page so you can look at them all before any flow is wired.
